primary_task: Drive a test-driven development cycle for a codebase, for example "Implement property-based testing strategy for complex business logic validation", writing failing tests, code that makes them pass, and refactoring.

requirements.name: language test framework (pytest/Jest/JUnit/NUnit/Go testing/Hypothesis/fast-check)
requirements.evidence: "Complete red-green-refactor cycle orchestration and enforcement"; "Testing framework expertise (JUnit, NUnit, pytest, Jest, Mocha, testing/T)" -- any one, matching the project language, satisfies it.
requirements.basis: "install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, npm, apt from Ubuntu, go modules, nuget, GitHub release downloads), build, test, run CLIs and scripts"

requirements.name: sub-agents
requirements.evidence: "3. **Orchestrate test workflows** across multiple agents and development streams"; "Orchestration of specialized testing agents (unit, integration, E2E)"
requirements.basis: "agent": "start sub-agents that work in parallel, send them messages and list them"

requirements.name: docker (containerized test environments)
requirements.evidence: "Cloud-native testing infrastructure and containerized test environments" (a capability, not a required step)
requirements.basis: "a Docker daemon (docker, docker compose and container builds cannot run)"

notes: Read as running tests in the session (red-green needs a runner), so a test framework is hard and installable. Other reading: if the request is the governance/metrics/coaching side ("Create cross-team TDD governance framework"), it is a writing task with no hard requirement; still ACHIEVABLE. Requests for containerized or cloud test environments, or MSBuild on Windows, would hit the lacking Docker daemon / Windows toolchains.
